## Shared context (verbatim, immutable)

# Verification-integrity re-review after V5 overload fixes

Read the complete origin/dev/v0.5.0..HEAD diff and all changed files read-only.
The previous Kiro findings kiro:0, kiro:1, and kiro:2 reported that Java, Python,
and TypeScript V5 missed self-comparisons with a trailing message argument. These
are settled fixes: all three scanners now compare the first two arguments whenever
at least two are present, and six new overload subtests failed before the fix and
pass after it. Verify those fixes but do not re-report them unless defective.

Look beyond the settled findings for concrete new defects in test deletion,
suppression, assertion weakening, parsing, baseline/move handling, CODEOWNERS
last-match coverage, CI base selection, and refactor behavior preservation.
Read only the files needed to validate a concern; do not run commands or tests and
do not enumerate documented heuristic limitations or optional refactors.

Return at most 3 findings with a concrete trigger and observable consequence.
If no new blocking defect is supported by the changed code, return an empty
findings list promptly.

summary: Reviewed the full 0e804a8b..393c6c11 diff introducing the verification-integrity gate (new scripts/check-verification-integrity.py, CODEOWNERS, CI job, contract doc, baseline-checker refactor, and unit tests). Verified the three settled V5 overload fixes: Java assertEquals/assertSame, Python assertEqual/assertIs, and TypeScript equal/strictEqual/deepEqual/deepStrictEqual now compare the first two arguments whenever at least two are present, each with matching subtests. Also re-examined the intermediate refactor commit (behavior-preserving extraction of call_arguments, parse_codeowner_entries, last_match_retains_owner, NON_EXCEPTIBLE_RULES), test deletion/rename/assertion-count comparison, content-hash move alignment, baseline subtraction for V3/V5 markers, CODEOWNERS last-match coverage including ownerless overrides and pattern translation, CI merge-base selection (consistent with the existing java-conventions and api-surface gates), fail-closed parsing paths, and the check-project-baseline.py refactor with its updated tests. No new defects with a concrete trigger and user-observable consequence were found beyond the heuristic limitations the contract explicitly documents.
